questions.knowledge_point: Finding a Parametrization of a Hyperboloid of Two Sheets
questions.problem:
The vector-valued function $f(\theta ,ϕ),$ given by

$$
f(\theta ,ϕ)=⟨\text{_____},\,\operatorname{cosh}⁡ϕ,\,2\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩
$$

parametrizes one sheet of the hyperboloid of two sheets defined in Cartesian coordinates as 

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{9}-{y}^{2}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{4}=-1.
$$

 

By first considering the transformations

$$
x=3X,\,y=Z,\,z=2Y
$$

and writing the resulting system in cylindrical polar coordinates, determine the first component of $f.$

*Hint: You may use the fact that the hyperbola ${Z}^{2}-{r}^{2}={k}^{2}$ can be parametrized as $⟨z,r⟩=⟨k\operatorname{cosh}⁡ϕ,k\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ⟩$* for $ϕ\in R.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, substituting the transformations

$$
x=3X,\,y=Z,\,z=2Y
$$

into our equation, we get

$$
{X}^{2}+{Y}^{2}-{Z}^{2}=-1.
$$

If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical coordinates of a point and $(X,Y,Z)$ are the corresponding Cartesian coordinates of that point, then we have

$$
X=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,Y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,Z=Z.
$$

Substituting this into our equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{X}^{2}+{Y}^{2}-{Z}^{2} & =-1 \\ (r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}-{Z}^{2} & =-1 \\ {r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )-{Z}^{2} & =-1 \\ {r}^{2}-{Z}^{2} & =-1 \\ {Z}^{2}-{r}^{2} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, the hyperbola ${Z}^{2}-{r}^{2}=1$ represents the intersection of our hyperboloid with the plane that passes through the $Z$-axis and makes the angle of $\theta $ with the positive $X$-axis. Using the hint, a parametrization of such hyperbola can be given as

$$
⟨Z,r⟩=⟨\operatorname{cosh}⁡ϕ,\,\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ⟩,\,ϕ\in R.
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\theta ,ϕ) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨3X,Z,2Y⟩ \\  & =⟨3r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,Z,\,2r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩ \\  & =⟨3(\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,\operatorname{cosh}⁡ϕ,\,2(\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩ \\  & =⟨3\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,\operatorname{cosh}⁡ϕ,\,2\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $\theta \in [0,2\pi )$ and $ϕ\in R.$

Therefore, the second component of $f$ is $3\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding a Polar Parametrization of a Paraboloid
questions.problem:
The vector-valued function $f(r,\theta ),$ given by

$$
f(r,\theta )=⟨5r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,\text{_____},\,{r}^{2}⟩
$$

parametrizes the elliptic paraboloid defined in Cartesian coordinates as 

$$
z=\frac{{x}^{2}}{25}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}.
$$

By first considering the transformations

$$
x=5X,\,y=2Y,\,z=Z
$$

and writing the resulting system in cylindrical polar coordinates, determine the second component of $f.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, substituting the transformations

$$
x=5X,\,y=2Y,\,z=Z
$$

into our equation, we get

$$
Z={X}^{2}+{Y}^{2}.
$$

If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical coordinates of a point and $(X,Y,Z)$ are the corresponding Cartesian coordinates of that point, then we have

$$
X=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,Y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,Z=z.
$$

Substituting this into our equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Z & ={X}^{2}+{Y}^{2} \\ Z & =(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2} \\ Z & ={r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ) \\ Z & ={r}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r,\theta ) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨5X,2Y,Z⟩ \\  & =⟨5r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,2r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,Z⟩ \\  & =⟨5r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,2r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,{r}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $r\in [0,\infty )$ and $\theta \in [0,2\pi ).$

Therefore, the second component of $f$ is $2r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .$

questions.problem:
The vector-valued function $f(r,\theta ),$ given by

$$
f(r,\theta )=⟨{r}^{2},\,\text{_____},\,4r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩
$$

parametrizes the elliptic paraboloid defined in Cartesian coordinates as

$$
x=\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{16}.
$$

By first considering the transformations

$$
x=Z,\,y=3X,\,z=4Y
$$

and writing the resulting system in cylindrical polar coordinates, determine the second component of $f.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, substituting the transformations

$$
x=Z,\,y=3X,\,z=4Y
$$

into our equation, we get

$$
Z={X}^{2}+{Y}^{2}.
$$

If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical coordinates of a point and $(X,Y,Z)$ are the corresponding Cartesian coordinates of that point, then we have

$$
X=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,Y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,Z=z.
$$

Substituting this into our equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Z & ={X}^{2}+{Y}^{2} \\ Z & =(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2} \\ Z & ={r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ) \\ Z & ={r}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r,\theta ) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨Z,3X,4Y⟩ \\  & =⟨Z,\,3r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,4r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩ \\  & =⟨{r}^{2},\,3r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,4r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $r\in [0,\infty )$ and $\theta \in [0,2\pi ).$

Therefore, the second component of $f$ is $3r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .$

questions.problem:
The vector-valued function $f(\theta ,ϕ),$ given by 

$$
f(\theta ,ϕ)=⟨2\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ,3\operatorname{cosh}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\text{_____}⟩
$$

parametrizes the hyperboloid of one sheet defined in Cartesian coordinates as 

$$
-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{25}=1.
$$

By first considering the transformations

$$
x=2Z,\,y=3Y,\,z=5X
$$

and writing the resulting system in cylindrical polar coordinates, determine the third component of $f.$

*Hint: You may use the fact that the hyperbola ${r}^{2}-{Z}^{2}={k}^{2}$ can be parametrized as $⟨r,Z⟩=⟨k\operatorname{cosh}⁡ϕ,k\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ⟩$* for $ϕ\in R.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, substituting the transformations

$$
x=2Z,\,y=3Y,\,z=5X
$$

into our equation, we get

$$
{X}^{2}+{Y}^{2}-{Z}^{2}=1.
$$

If $(r,\theta ,Z)$ are the cylindrical coordinates of a point and $(X,Y,Z)$ are the corresponding Cartesian coordinates of that point, then we have

$$
X=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,Y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,Z=Z.
$$

Substituting this into our equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{X}^{2}+{Y}^{2}-{Z}^{2} & =1 \\ (r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}-{Z}^{2} & =1 \\ {r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )-{Z}^{2} & =1 \\ {r}^{2}-{Z}^{2} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, the hyperbola ${r}^{2}-{Z}^{2}=1$ represents the intersection of our hyperboloid with the plane that passes through the $Z$-axis and makes the angle of $\theta $ with the positive $X$-axis. Using the hint, a parametrization of such hyperbola can be given as

$$
⟨r,Z⟩=⟨\operatorname{cosh}⁡ϕ,\,\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ⟩,\,ϕ\in R.
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\theta ,ϕ) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨2Z,3Y,5X⟩ \\  & =⟨2Z,\,3r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,5r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ,\,3(\operatorname{cosh}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,5(\operatorname{cosh}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ,\,3\operatorname{cosh}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,5\operatorname{cosh}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $\theta \in [0,2\pi )$ and $ϕ\in R.$

Therefore, the third component of $f$ is $5\operatorname{cosh}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .$
